test_title: SSC Stenographer 2025 Official Paper (Held On: 06 Aug, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
Choose the correct direct speech form of the following sentence.

He asked me whether I had taken the medications.

options.text: He said, "Whether you take the medications?"
He said, "Did you take the medications?"
He said, "Did I take the medications?"
He said, "Did you took the medications?"

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indirect Speech:** He asked me whether I had taken the medications.
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **"whether I had taken" becomes "Did you take"**
 
 
• Indirect question "whether I had taken" is converted to direct question "Did you take."
 
• Pronoun "I" is changed to "you" to match direct speech.
 
• Verb "had taken" is changed to "take" to match simple past tense in direct questions.
 
 
 
• **Reporting verb:**
 
 
• Indirect: "asked"
 
• Converted to: "said," maintaining the questioning tone.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Punctuation and Format:**
 
 
• Direct speech is enclosed in quotation marks.
 
• Starts with a capital letter "Did" and ends with a question mark "?".
 
• Reporting clause follows the quoted speech, starting with a lowercase letter after the comma.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "Whether you take the medications?"

 
 
• Incorrect phrasing: "Whether" is not used in direct speech questions.
 
 
 
• **Option 3:** "Did I take the medications?"
 
 
• Pronoun "I" is incorrect in context; should be "you" to match the speaker and listener roles.
 
 
 
• **Option 4:** "Did you took the medications?"
 
 
• Incorrect verb form: "took" should be "take" in simple past tense questions.
